title: QAOA for Max-Cut
summary: Max-Cut on a 5-vertex graph with a two-layer QAOA.
objectives: Build QAOA layers from a cost layer (IsingZZ on the edges) and a mixer layer (RX on every qubit)
Optimize the angles until the approximation ratio of the Max-Cut solution exceeds 0.85
Explain why one layer is not enough for this graph and more layers raise the best achievable ratio
mission: Divide the 5 vertices of the graph into two groups so that as many edges as possible are cut. Build a QAOA circuit with cost layers (IsingZZ on the edges) and mixer layers (RX on every qubit), and optimize the angles until the approximation ratio exceeds 0.85.

prediction.question: With one layer (p = 1) and the best possible angles, does the approximation ratio for this graph exceed 0.85?
options: Yes, one layer is always enough
No, the best ratio is about 0.82
prediction.explanation: For p = 1 the best ratio on this graph is about 0.82. Each additional layer adds two angles and cannot lower the best achievable ratio; for p = 2 it is about 0.92.

hints: In layer(gamma, beta): for each edge (i, j) in edges apply qml.IsingZZ(gamma, wires=[i, j]); then apply qml.RX(2 * beta, wires=wire) on each qubit.
The circuit applies a Hadamard to each of the 5 qubits, then one layer for each pair (gamma, beta) in params. It returns qml.expval(cost_h), which the optimizer minimizes.
Use params of shape (2, 2), that is p = 2 layers, and optimizer = qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1) for about 80 steps, appending circuit(params) to history at each step.
